title: Quadratic features left most IT variance unexplained by 25 V4 sites in one macaque
abstract: We tested whether quadratic functions of V4 responses recover IT signal that a linear read-out misses. We used the public Majaj/Hong 2015 data from one macaque, with 25 disjoint predictor and target sites per area. Eight outer folds held out whole objects. A separate repeat set selected the ridge penalty. Two other repeat sets gave a noise-corrected explained variance score (FEV). Across 24 draws of 640 images and sites, V4-to-IT FEV rose from 0.109 to 0.115. The gain was 0.007, with a mean plus or minus 1.96 SD range of -0.007 to 0.021. Reverse and within-area gains were also small. In an exploratory check with all 2,560 images, the forward quadratic gain was 0.021; diagonal squares added 0.009. Thus these response-energy models did not close the forward read-out gap in this sample. The test puts a measured limit on these feature models in a macaque sample that had no mouse-like spectral compression. Limits include one animal, sparse multi-unit populations, noisy source features, fixed feature-block weights, and a restricted model class. Draw ranges are sensitivity measures, not confidence intervals over animals.
